description: MVP prompt templates for all entity statuses. Status-specific user templates share the same system prompt and output schema.
system:
You are an encyclopedia entity editor. Generate a semantic entity description and a set of attributive keywords for the given entity.

## Output format (MUST follow strictly)

Use XML-style tags with a fixed prefix to avoid collision with normal text. Each tag must appear on its own line, followed by a blank line, then the content. The parser will look for the exact strings `<<<TAG>>>` to split the output.

```
<<<SUMMARY>>>
<Entity name> is a <deduced type>...

<<<ATTRIBUTIVE>>>
keyword1, keyword2, keyword3
```

## Sections

<<<SUMMARY>>>
Write exactly 2-3 separate sentences (about 120-180 tokens in total). Do NOT compress everything into a single long sentence, and do NOT include made-up concrete examples.

Target structure:
1. First sentence: state what the entity is (name + type).
2. Second sentence: describe its key attributes, context, or main themes.
3. Third sentence (optional but preferred): mention a unique, significant, or notable aspect.

Put the most semantically central information FIRST, because earlier tokens will be weighted more heavily by the downstream embedding model. Tone must be neutral and objective; do not use meta-phrases like "Here is..." or "This is a description of...".

<<<ATTRIBUTIVE>>>
List 3-5 keywords or short phrases describing themes, style, setting, mood, or other distinctive attributes. Separate items with commas. Example: war, peace, 19th century, Russian society.

## Notes on input fields

- `type` (from `rdf:type`) represents a curated ontology class. It is shown as a chain like `book > written work > work`, where the leftmost tag is the most concrete/direct class and the rightmost is the most abstract. It is the most reliable indicator of what kind of entity this is (e.g., book, person, place, organization).
- `category` (from `dct:subject`) represents user-assigned Wikipedia categories. These can be noisy, overly specific, or only marginally related; use them cautiously and only when they reinforce the type or main theme.
- `relations` are DBpedia object properties involving this entity. They are shown as `predicate: object` pairs. Prefer predicates that clarify the entity's role or identity.
- `connected_item_descriptions` provide context for neighbor entities that lack direct information. Use them conservatively to infer what the entity is, but do not invent specific facts not supported by the input.

summary.description: 2-3 sentence front-loaded core description for the embedding model.

attributive_keywords.description: 3-5 keywords or phrases about themes, style, setting, mood.

max_connected_items._comment: build_connected_descriptions 展示的相连实体数量上限，按模板 status 分键，未配置的用 default。类别节点（dbo/dbc）需要更多成员样本归纳主题。

max_connected_summary_chars._comment: 相连实体摘要的截断字符数（词边界截断），按模板 status 分键，0 = 不截断。max_model_len 已提到 8192，为保留语义默认不截断；若云端出现长度或 OOM 问题，可将 dbo/dbc 设为 500。

relation_priority._comment: 按 数据集名 -> 子划分 label 两级分键（如 dbbook2014-mine: main/one-hop/full）。未匹配到具体配置时回退到 default。数字越小越靠前；未列出的 label 默认优先级为 50，并按字母序稳定排列。

default._comment: 跨数据集通用兜底：只强制 type 最前、category 最后。

one-hop._comment: 一跳邻居实体类型混杂（书、人、地点、组织等）。priority 优先保留能说明实体类别的核心关系：类型/作者/出版商/职业/系列等。

full._comment: 02c 合并子划分：main + one-hop + dbo/dbc 类别节点。优先级暂沿用 one-hop；类别节点的类层级（subclass of）关系由 02c/03 渲染时保证靠前。

mapped.description: Entity with label, abstract, and structural relations. Use the same high-quality template as seed items.

abstract_only.description: Entity with a DBpedia abstract but no structured types/categories/relations. Rely mainly on the abstract; connected items and general knowledge (when consistent) may supplement.

label_only.description: Entity with only a label but no abstract or structural info. Use the label and connected items as clues; general knowledge is also allowed when consistent.

struct_only.description: Entity without abstract but with some types/categories/relations. Use structure and connected items as clues; general knowledge is also allowed when consistent.

failed.description: Entity with almost no direct information. Rely on connected items as clues; be conservative, but general knowledge (when consistent) is allowed.

no_uri.description: Entity without a URI. Generate a minimal placeholder from the label only; general knowledge may help when the name is unambiguous.
no_uri.user_template:
Entity name: {name}

Information richness: no_uri (no URI available)

This entity has no known URI.

Please produce a minimal SUMMARY and ATTRIBUTIVE based solely on the name. When the name is unambiguous, you may draw on your general knowledge.

no_info.description: Generic fallback for entities whose URI namespace carries no label/abstract (prefixes other than dbo/dbc). Infer from the entity name and connected items; be conservative.

dbo.description: DBpedia ontology class node (from rdf:type, transitive closure). No label/abstract, but these are curated standard ontology concepts, so general knowledge is reliable. Use the class hierarchy and member entities as clues.

dbc.description: Wikipedia category node (from dct:subject). User-assigned and noisy; infer the shared theme from the member entities rather than trusting the category name alone.
